event_title: Best Chinese AI Company end of November?
question: Will any other company have the best Chinese AI model at the end of November 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the company that owns the model that has the highest arena rank among primarily Chinese companies, based on the arena.ai Text Arena (Overall) when the table under the "Leaderboard" tab is checked on November 30, 2026, 12:00 PM ET.

Chinese Companies include but are not limited to Alibaba, Moonshot, Baidu, Z.ai, Xiaomi, DeepSeek, ByteDance, MiniMax, Meituan, Tencent, and StepFun. Companies not headquartered in China or not primarily owned or operating within the Chinese technology ecosystem are not considered primarily Chinese.

Results from the "Rank" column under the "Text Arena | Overall" Leaderboard tab at https://arena.ai/leaderboard/text/overall-no-style-control with style control off (Adjustments: None) and filtered for "Models" will be used to resolve this market.

Note: Models marked “AutoEval” at the applicable check time will not be considered, regardless of whether they display a rank or score.

Qualifying Chinese Models will be ordered primarily by their leaderboard rank at the market’s check time. If two or more models are tied on rank, they will be ordered by their Arena score, including any underlying, unrounded, granular values reflected in the data below the leaderboard. If a tie still remains, alphabetical order of company names as listed in this market group will be used as a final tiebreaker (e.g., if the two models are tied by exact arena score, “Meituan” would be ranked ahead of “Xiaomi”). This market will resolve based on the company that occupies first place under this ranking.

The resolution source for this market is the arena.ai Text Arena (Overall). If this resolution source is unavailable at check time, this market will remain open until the leaderboard comes back online and will resolve based on the first check after it becomes available. If it becomes permanently unavailable, this market will resolve to "Other".
bucket_reason: This question is about AI company competition and technology rankings, not interstate conflict.

This market will resolve according to the company that owns the model that has the highest arena rank among primarily Chinese companies, based on the arena.ai Text Arena (Overall) when the table under the "Leaderboard" tab is checked on December 31, 2026, 12:00 PM ET.

Chinese Companies include but are not limited to Alibaba, Moonshot, Baidu, Z.ai, Xiaomi, DeepSeek, ByteDance, MiniMax, Meituan, Tencent, and StepFun. Companies not headquartered in China or not primarily owned or operating within the Chinese technology ecosystem are not considered primarily Chinese.

Results from the "Rank" column under the "Text Arena | Overall" Leaderboard tab at https://arena.ai/leaderboard/text/overall-no-style-control with style control off (Adjustments: None) and filtered for "Models" will be used to resolve this market.

Note: Models marked “AutoEval” at the applicable check time will not be considered, regardless of whether they display a rank or score.

Qualifying Chinese Models will be ordered primarily by their leaderboard rank at the market’s check time. If two or more models are tied on rank, they will be ordered by their Arena score, including any underlying, unrounded, granular values reflected in the data below the leaderboard. If a tie still remains, alphabetical order of company names as listed in this market group will be used as a final tiebreaker (e.g., if the two models are tied by exact arena score, “Meituan” would be ranked ahead of “Xiaomi”). This market will resolve based on the company that occupies first place under this ranking.

The resolution source for this market is the arena.ai Text Arena (Overall). If this resolution source is unavailable at check time, this market will remain open until the leaderboard comes back online and will resolve based on the first check after it becomes available. If it becomes permanently unavailable, this market will resolve to "Other".
bucket_reason: This question is about AI company rankings, not interstate conflict between state actors.

event_title: November Inflation China - Monthly
question: Will China's monthly inflation increase by ≥0.4% in November?
description:
This is a market about the monthly variation of consumer prices in China as reported by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) of China.

This market will resolve according to the number the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased by in November 2026 (% change from the previous month) according to the monthly NBS report.

The resolution source for this market will be the NBS Consumer Price Index monthly report released for November 2026 (https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/), currently scheduled to be released in December 2026. Resolution of this market will take place upon release of the aforementioned data. If no data for the specified month is released by the date the next month's data is scheduled to be released, this market will resolve based on data from the last available month.

You can find the relevant figure by locating the report for November 2026 on the Press Releases page (see: https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/), locating the table named "Consumer Price Index in November 2026", and finding the consumer price index figure in the column labeled "Growth Rate M/M (%)".

Note: the resolution source for this market will be the official monthly NBS CPI news release which reports monthly inflation to only one decimal point (e.g. 1.9%). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market. For the full release schedule, see: https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/ReleaseCalendar/
bucket_reason: This question is about China's domestic economic inflation data, not interstate conflict between state actors.

event_title: Taipei Mayor Election Winner
question: Will Candidate A win the next Taipei Mayor election?
description:
Taiwanese local elections are scheduled to be held on November 28, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next Mayor of Taipei as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder Mayors appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known, or no candidate has been elected, by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Taiwanese government, specifically the Central Election Commission (https://db.cec.gov.tw/).
bucket_reason: This is a municipal election question, not about interstate conflict onset between two state actors.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next Mayor of Tainan as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder Mayors appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known, or no candidate has been elected, by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Taiwanese government, specifically the Central Election Commission (https://db.cec.gov.tw/).
bucket_reason: This is a local municipal election question, not about interstate conflict between state actors.

description:
Taiwanese local elections are scheduled to be held on November 28, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next Magistrate of Taitung County as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder Magistrates appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known, or no candidate has been elected, by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Taiwanese government, specifically the Central Election Commission (https://db.cec.gov.tw/).
bucket_reason: This is a local election question in Taiwan with no direct connection to interstate conflict onset between state actors.

Taiwanese local elections are scheduled to be held on November 28, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next Magistrate of Penghu County as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder Magistrates appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known, or no candidate has been elected, by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Taiwanese government, specifically the Central Election Commission (https://db.cec.gov.tw/).
bucket_reason: This is a local election question about a Taiwanese county magistrate race, not about interstate conflict.

event_title: 2026 Taipei Mayoral Election: Margin of Victory
question: Will Chiang Wan-an win the 2026 Taipei Mayoral Election by between 8% and 12%?
description:
The 2026 Taipei mayoral election is scheduled to take place on November 28, 2026, to elect the next mayor of Taipei.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the specified election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first-place and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If two or more candidates tie for the most valid votes in this election, and the tie is between two candidates listed, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the candidate whose listed last name comes first in alphabetical order. If the tie is between a listed candidate and an unlisted candidate, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the listed candidate. If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to “Other.”

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the election results are not known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Taiwanese government, specifically the Central Election Commission (https://db.cec.gov.tw/).

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.
bucket_reason: This is about a municipal election outcome and margin of victory, not about interstate conflict between state actors.

event_title: 2026 Taiwanese Mayoral Elections: Party Winner
question: Will another party win the most mayoral elections in the 2026 Taiwan local elections?
description:
Taiwanese local elections are scheduled to be held on November 28, 2026. 

This market will resolve according to the party whose official candidates win the most mayoral elections for Taiwan’s special municipalities and cities during these elections.

A candidate will be considered an official candidate of a party if they are officially nominated by that party and are registered for the relevant election in affiliation with that party. Independent candidates will not count for any party.

Taiwan’s local governments include the following cities and special municipalities:

Cities/special municipalities (mayoral elections): Taipei City, New Taipei City, Taoyuan City, Taichung City, Tainan City, Kaohsiung City, Keelung City, Hsinchu City, Chiayi City

Only elections for the listed cities or special municipalities will be counted for this market. A party will have won as soon as it becomes mathematically impossible for any other party to equal or surpass its number of wins in these elections.

In the case of a tie between two or more parties for the greatest number of relevant mayoral elections won, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose English name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group.

Resolution of this market will be based on the results of the relevant elections, once those results are official. This market will remain open until a party has won or until the results of all of the relevant elections are made official. If the results of any of the relevant 2026 Taiwanese local elections aren’t known by June 30, 2027 11:59 PM ET, the winning party will be determined based on the available results up to that point. If none of the results of the relevant 2026 Taiwanese local elections are known by that time, this market will resolve to “Other”.

event_title: Russia-Ukraine-EU Trilateral Diplomatic Meeting by...?
question: Next Russia-Ukraine-EU Trilateral Diplomatic Meeting by December 31, 2026?
description:
On November 10–11, 2026, Russian and Ukrainian delegations led by Vladimir Medinsky and Rustem Umerov held US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi (see: https://kyivindependent.com/ukraine-russia-us-resume-trilateral-peace-talks-in-abu-dhabi-after-9-month-pause/). Senior officials from the European Union, France, Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom were also in Abu Dhabi and met with US and Ukrainian representatives, while Russia stated that its delegation had no contact with European officials.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a senior-level diplomatic meeting between Russia, Ukraine, and the European Union (EU) between market creation and the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of Russia, Ukraine, and the EU who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or institutions deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A meeting will qualify only if senior-level representatives of all three participate in the same meeting session while physically present together; meetings conducted through translators qualify. Presence in the same city, venue, or facility will not suffice, and separate or parallel meetings in which EU representatives meet with only one of Russia or Ukraine (e.g., EU officials meeting with Ukrainian and US representatives on the sidelines of Russia-Ukraine talks) will not qualify. EU officials will count as participants whether they take part as a negotiating party, mediator or facilitator, provided they actively take part in the meeting session itself; officials who only host, welcome, or provide logistical support for a meeting will not be considered participants. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, prisoner exchange, or further engagement.

A meeting qualifies regardless of its subject matter, including meetings limited to humanitarian issues (e.g., prisoner exchanges, the return of civilians or children, or humanitarian pauses), whether or not broader Russia-Ukraine peace terms, such as a ceasefire, peace agreement, territorial issues, security guarantees, or similar, are discussed. Officials of other countries or organizations (e.g., the US or NATO) do not count as representatives of Russia, Ukraine, or the EU.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level only if each of Russia, Ukraine and the EU is represented by at least one senior official. For Russia and Ukraine, a senior official is a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. For the EU, a senior official is the President of the European Commission, the President of the European Council, the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, or another individual designated by one of them to represent the EU in the negotiations. The EU will be considered represented only by officials acting on behalf of the EU's institutions; officials of individual EU member states or other European countries (e.g., France, Germany or the United Kingdom) will not count as EU representatives. The participation of other parties (e.g., the US) will not prevent a meeting from qualifying. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations or to represent the EU in the negotiations. Ukraine's Parliamentary Commissioner for Human Rights and Russia's High Commissioner for Human Rights will not be considered senior-level representatives. Qualifying individuals include, regardless of their position: for Russia, Vladimir Putin, Sergei Lavrov, Yuri Ushakov, Vladimir Medinsky, Igor Kostyukov, Kirill Dmitriev, Sergei Ryabkov, Mikhail Galuzin, Alexander Fomin and Yuri Zhigarlovsky; for Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelensky, Andrii Sybiha, Rustem Umerov, Kyrylo Budanov, Serhiy Kyslytsya, Davyd Arakhamia, Andrii Hnatov and Vadym Skibitsky; and for the EU, Ursula von der Leyen, António Costa, Kaja Kallas, Björn Seibert and Anna-Maria Boura. In each case, the senior official must take part in the meeting itself.

Sessions, proceedings, or convenings of standing international organizations, treaty bodies, or recurring multilateral summits or conferences (e.g., the United Nations General Assembly, G7, and G20 summits) do not qualify, unless a qualifying and deliberate diplomatic meeting between representatives of Russia, Ukraine, and the EU is separately held alongside such a convening.

The following do not qualify: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present together; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments or institutions.

The occurrence of a qualifying meeting must be confirmed by the resolution sources by the resolution date.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Russia and Ukraine and the European Union, and a consensus of credible reporting.
bucket_reason: This concerns diplomatic negotiations between state actors related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, but asks about a meeting occurrence rather than conflict onset or escalation directly.

event_title: Russia x Ukraine major prisoner exchange by...?
question: Russia x Ukraine major prisoner exchange by December 31, 2026?
description:
On November 11, 2026, following US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, Russia and Ukraine agreed in principle to a large-scale exchange of prisoners of war, with the number of prisoners involved still being finalized.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if a confirmed major prisoner exchange between Russia and Ukraine takes place between market creation and the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A prisoner exchange refers to a reciprocal transfer in which each country releases to the other at least one living individual held in its custody. Exchanges conducted with the assistance of third parties (e.g., mediation by the United Arab Emirates or the United States, or a handover in Belarus) will qualify.

A prisoner exchange is major if at least 1,000 individuals in total, counting those released by both countries combined, are released as part of it (e.g., an exchange of 500 for 500). The numbers released by each side need not be equal. Military and civilian detainees held by either government who are released as part of the exchange will be counted. Releases on different days count as one prisoner exchange only if the government of Russia, the government of Ukraine, or a consensus of credible reporting describes them as stages of the same agreed exchange (e.g., the 500-for-500 exchange on March 5–6, 2026). Releases held more than 7 calendar days (ET) after the previous release count as a separate exchange regardless of how they are framed by Russia, Ukraine, or credible reporting. Only releases completed between market creation and the listed date count toward the total.

The following will not qualify as an exchange or count toward the total: the repatriation of bodies or remains; unilateral releases; and transfers of individuals not held in detention, such as family reunifications, humanitarian evacuations, or the return of children. An agreement or announcement of a future exchange will not qualify unless the exchange actually takes place.

The number of individuals released will be used as communicated by the governments of Russia or Ukraine, including where summed across multiple releases in a single exchange. Where a government reports only the individuals it received or released, the number released by each side will be combined from both governments' communications. If the two governments report conflicting figures for the same side, the lower figure will be used. If the number of released individuals cannot be determined from official government communications, a consensus of credible reporting will be used.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Russia and Ukraine and a consensus of credible reporting.
bucket_reason: A prisoner exchange is a diplomatic/military event between two state actors at war, but it concerns a specific negotiated outcome rather than conflict onset or escalation.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the FAA, the U.S. Department of Transportation, or their authorized representatives officially announce that this nationwide ground stop is no longer in effect between market creation and the listed date and time (inclusive of the listed minute). Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must communicate that the nationwide (all-airports) ground stop is cancelled or otherwise no longer in effect, including where it is replaced by narrower ground stops or other traffic management initiatives at individual airports or regions. Announcements that the ground stop is lifted for, or does not affect, specific airports, regions, or flights while the nationwide ground stop remains in effect will not count.

An announcement that the ground stop will end at a future time will not qualify until its effective time.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the FAA & the Department of Transportation; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
bucket_reason: This question is about FAA air traffic management, not interstate conflict between state actors.
